definition.description: Travel forward in a clear lane using a relaxed alternating left-right step-hop skip with quiet low-amplitude contacts, upright posture, and reciprocal arm action. A pass ends at the declared finish under control. This is not A-skip, running, bounding, a maximal power skip, a cone-spacing task, a ball task, or a single-leg cycle drill.

environment.surface: level dry non-slip forgiving surface with a declared 8-20 metre lane and protected finish
environment.space: one athlete at a time; no cross traffic
inspection: surface and footwear support quiet low-amplitude contacts
communication and exit route are clear
environment.changeRule: Changing contact sequence, amplitude, intent, lane, cue, object, external spacing, cadence, or finish requires full identity and workout revalidation.

selectionPrerequisites: can repeat an alternating step-hop sequence at relaxed submaximal intent
safe lane, finish, surface, footwear, and communication
current symptoms and contact budget fit
understands stop signal and controlled finish
excludeOrEscalate: symptom, unsafe surface, lane, finish, footwear, communication, or contact-budget conflict
pain, limp, repeated stumble, dizziness, neurologic, circulation, breathing, chest, balance, or communication concern
notEstablishedByEvidence: a universal readiness level, cadence, contact volume, recovery dose, sprint transfer, or outcome claim

provenance.identityAuthority: Source 104 plus skipping-fast-leg-drills-v1 evidence packet; cadence and pass length are delivery annotations only.

anatomy.laterality: alternating left-right step-hop cycles through the full pass
anatomy.claimsBoundary: Task mechanics only; no diagnosis, treatment, injury-prevention, or sprint-performance claim.

athleteSupport.whyItMatters: Candidate low-to-moderate rhythm and coordination exposure when this exact relaxed step-hop task fits the workout.
athleteSupport.primaryCue: Step-hop and alternate; stay tall, relaxed, quiet, and finish under control.
secondaryCues: opposite arm and leg move together
keep the bounce low and forward
do not stretch contacts or chase speed
expectedSensations: light repeated foot, calf, hip, and trunk effort
unexpectedSensations: pain, limping, repeated stumble, dizziness, or inability to control the finish
selfChecks: both sides keep the same step-hop rhythm
posture and arm action remain relaxed

observationChecklist: left-right rhythm, arm action, posture, amplitude, contact sound, and first quality loss
actual passes, distance, contacts, rest, symptoms, and stop reason

faultCorrections.turns_into_running_or_a_skip: slow the pass, restore the relaxed step-hop rhythm, or select a separately reviewed task
faultCorrections.loud_or_reaching_contacts: shorten the lane or reduce amplitude and end the set if quiet contacts do not return
faultCorrections.lost_alternation: reset at a slower cadence; do not count an incomplete sequence

doNotUseWhen: a maximal power skip, A-skip, bound, run, cone-spacing, ball, or single-leg cycle task is intended
the lane, finish, surface, footwear, or communication is unsafe
the task conflicts with symptoms or contact budget

supportOperations.supportEscalation: Stop unresolved symptom, surface, identity, or quality concerns.
supportOperations.changeImpactPolicy: Any change to task identity, cue, lane, surface, dose, or substitution reruns selection, logistics, duration, fatigue, and validation.

snapshot.description: Athlete skips forward with relaxed rhythm, tall posture, and coordinated opposite arm-leg action.

requirements.contactRule: repeat the relaxed alternating step-hop pattern for the declared pass

contactExposureModel.per_set_range: record total and per-side step-hop contacts or pass distance

deliveryProfiles.purpose: Candidate low-volume relaxed alternating step-hop preparation when the exact lane, contact, and finish contract fits.

dosage.countRule: record only controlled full passes with the alternating step-hop sequence

deliveryProfiles.qualityGate: The alternating step-hop sequence, reciprocal arms, tall relaxed posture, quiet contacts, low amplitude, and controlled finish remain repeatable.
stopRules: stop on pain, limp, repeated stumble, unsafe lane, unsafe finish, or participant request
stop when rhythm, quiet contacts, posture, alternation, or controlled finish cannot be restored
deliveryProfiles.coachInstructions: Declare the lane, finish, intent, and count rule; demonstrate one relaxed pass and stop before speed or fatigue changes the task.
deliveryProfiles.athleteInstructions: Step-hop and alternate with quiet low contacts, relaxed arms, and a controlled finish.
deliveryProfiles.expectedAdaptation: Candidate preparation only; no outcome is guaranteed.

doseScaling.reduce: shorter lane, fewer passes, lower amplitude, slower cadence, longer rest, or a separately reviewed task
doseScaling.doNotAutoProgress: Do not add maximal projection, A-skip mechanics, external spacing, a ball task, sprint exit, or a single-leg cycle without revalidation.

supportPrompts.athlete: Relaxed step-hop, alternate, and finish under control.
supportPrompts.coach: Speed is not a hidden progression.

legacy.loadNote: Candidate-only; record passes, distance or contacts, cadence, surface, and symptoms.

legacy.coachLanguage: Use the exact candidate only after lane, finish, contact-budget, duration, and downstream-demand checks.

safety.prerequisiteNotes: Readiness is the exact relaxed skip, lane, finish, surface, symptoms, contact budget, dose, and downstream task—not a participant classification.
readinessChecks: confirm lane, finish, surface, footwear, and stop signal
confirm relaxed alternating step-hop and controlled finish
confirm contact budget and symptoms fit
stopSigns: dizziness, chest, breathing, neurologic, or circulation symptoms
unsafe lane, stumble, loud contacts, rhythm loss, or uncontrolled finish
contraindications: a distinct A-skip, run, bound, maximal power skip, cone, ball, or single-leg cycle intent
commonSubstitutions: Use another reviewed task only after revalidation.
Do not treat an A-skip, run, bound, power skip, cone drill, ball task, or single-leg cycle as an automatic substitution.
